papers.title: Aperiodic dynamics track cortical state shifts during sleep K-complexes.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Used time-resolved spectral parameterization of overnight sleep EEG to disentangle aperiodic dynamics from waveform artifacts around expert-annotated K-complexes. After controls, a component of the K-complex-locked aperiodic change survived, suggesting that K-complexes are accompanied by a genuine shift toward a higher-exponent, inhibition-dominated cortical state.

papers.title: Partial sleep deprivation diminishes and uncouples neuronal activity and energy metabolism in the live mouse hippocampus.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Longitudinally monitored spontaneous neuronal activity and tissue partial pressure of oxygen (pO2) in the live mouse hippocampus CA1 using two-photon microscopy before, during, and after 7 days of partial sleep deprivation. Partial sleep deprivation produced a progressive decline in spontaneous neural activity and sustained elevation in tissue pO2, with neuronal activity failing to return to baseline and oxygenation continuing to increase after 7 days of recovery.

papers.title: Using the aperiodic slope across learning to predict sleep-based memory consolidation
papers.summary: Tested whether EEG aperiodic slope changes across learning and a nap predict sleep-based memory consolidation in 27 participants who learned object-word pairs. A shift toward inhibition during learning was beneficial for memory accuracy only in the nap condition, and a shift toward inhibition across learning followed by a shift toward excitation during nap predicted reduced N400 amplitudes.

papers.title: Hyperexcitable but seizure-free: hippocampal network dysfunction in a Wolfram syndrome model.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Characterized hippocampal function across scales in mice carrying a patient orthologous Wfs1 variant (p.W542*) to model Wolfram syndrome. Mutant mice showed loss of excitatory synapses and cellular hyperexcitability without increased network bursting or seizures, alongside male-specific reduction in hippocampal low-gamma power, impaired fear memory, and reduced voluntary motor activity.

papers.title: A Computational Model Captures Orexin-Dependent Modulation of Memory Consolidation.
papers.summary: A rate-based computational model links orexinergic tone-dependent sharp-wave ripple statistics to memory performance, combining an encoding module with an OX2R-driven consolidation module. The model predicts task-dependent effects: encoding-dominant learning benefits from increasing orexin drive, whereas consolidation-dominant learning is non-monotonic with an internal optimum, and effective consolidation depends on task complexity reflected in sequence length.

papers.title: The Bern Sleep-Wake Registry: A 25-year multimodal resource for data-driven sleep medicine
papers.summary: Describes the Bern Sleep-Wake Registry, a 25-year multimodal resource integrating clinical information, questionnaire scores, objective sleep-wake assessments, and raw signal data from patients referred to a tertiary sleep center. As of September 2025, the registry includes records from over 11,000 patients with more than 12,000 polysomnographies and other objective tests, supporting investigation of disease trajectories and biomarkers in sleep medicine.

papers.title: When Charon Knocks at the Sleep Laboratory: Are European Heatwaves an Underrecognized Methodological Challenge for Sleep Research?
papers.summary: This letter raises the concern that European heatwaves are an underrecognized methodological challenge for sleep research, potentially confounding laboratory-based sleep studies and their interpretation.

papers.title: P-body sequestration of clock transcripts delays repressor synthesis to set circadian period in Drosophila.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using time-resolved miniTurbo proximity labeling of PER across four circadian phases in Drosophila clock neurons, the authors defined a 252-protein PER proximitome and identified P-body components Me31B (DDX6) and Pacman (Pcm; XRN1) as circadian regulators. They show that per and tim transcripts localize to Me31B-labeled P-bodies and are poorly translated, with Me31B knockdown releasing per mRNA from P-bodies and causing earlier and ~2-fold higher PER accumulation, while Me31B overexpression delays PER accumulation and lengthens free-running period by ~2 h.

papers.title: Chronic Social Isolation Reshapes the Metabolome in Drosophila.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study performed untargeted metabolomic profiling in Drosophila after chronic social isolation and found a distinct metabolomic signature spanning amino acids, carbohydrates, and lipids. The result provides a metabolomic foundation for understanding physiological consequences of social isolation, building on prior evidence that isolation reduces sleep and increases feeding.

papers.title: NOD1 contributes to reduced postoperative memory performance induced by preoperative sleep deprivation and anesthesia/surgery in mice.
papers.summary: In mice with preoperative acute sleep deprivation and/or anesthesia/surgery, the study found reduced postoperative memory performance accompanied by increased hippocampal CA1 NOD1 expression, elevated p-p65/p65 ratio, Iba1-related changes, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and increased ileal lysozyme. Iba1 promoter-driven NOD1 knockdown improved memory performance, while Lyz1 deficiency improved OLMT and Y-maze performance, implicating hippocampal CA1 NOD1 and gut-related alterations in postoperative memory impairment.

papers.title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing and Sleep Fragmentation in Relation to Atrial Fibrillation Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 cohort studies (611,898 participants) found that sleep-disordered breathing was associated with increased incident atrial fibrillation risk (RR 1.67, 95% CI 1.41-1.97) and recurrent AF (RR 1.55, 95% CI 1.40-1.72), with a dose-response relationship showing a 2% increase in AF risk per unit rise in apnea-hypopnea index. The authors conclude that sleep disturbances are significantly associated with both incident and recurrent AF and may be modifiable risk factors.

papers.title: The development of slow and fast theta oscillations in the human brain.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Analyzing intracranial EEG from 101 children and adults across task-based and resting-state conditions, this preregistered study characterized slow (~1.5-4.5 Hz) and fast (~4.5-9.0 Hz) theta oscillations across widespread brain regions. It found distinct slow and fast theta with a posterior-to-anterior spatial gradient, a peak dissociation between the two during young adulthood, and that individual differences in task-based slow theta frequencies predicted memory performance, linking hippocampal and prefrontal slow theta maturation to attention and memory development.

papers.title: What drives intersubject correlation of EEG during auditory narratives?
papers.summary: Using temporal response functions and correlated component analysis on EEG from participants listening to auditory narratives under passive, attentive, and distracted conditions, the study assessed contributions of acoustic and linguistic features to intersubject correlation. Acoustic features explained more variance and were the main ISC contributors, attention-related ISC increases involved all features, and word surprisal affected ISC only during active engagement, with a small overall portion explained by linear TRF responses.

papers.title: Neonatal Pain Assessment After Night Shifts in NICU Professionals: A Within-Subject Exploratory Eye-Tracking Study.
papers.summary: In a within-subject eye-tracking study, 20 experienced NICU professionals rated pain in 42 standardized neonatal video clips after rest versus after night shifts. Pain ratings and pupillary responses did not differ significantly, but exploratory eye-tracking suggested reduced visual exploration after night shifts, with the authors cautioning that these secondary findings are hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: The circadian clock regulates KCNH2 (hERG) promoter activity through daily temperature rhythms.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using luciferase reporter constructs for the conserved human KCNH2 promoter in C2C12 myotubes, this study tested whether daily temperature cycles drive circadian promoter activity. Temperature cycling produced sustained oscillations dependent on a conserved tandem E-box and BMAL1:CLOCK, and dominant-negative CLOCKΔ19 reduced promoter amplitude, indicating that the circadian clock regulates KCNH2 promoter activity through daily temperature rhythms.

papers.title: Intrinsic circadian organization of the spinal cord and dorsal root ganglia.
papers.summary: Real-time bioluminescence imaging showed tissue-autonomous PER2 oscillations in the spinal dorsal horn and dorsal root ganglia, and RNA sequencing across a 52-hour circadian time course identified 626 rhythmic DRG genes with nonuniform temporal clustering. The findings establish the spinal dorsal horn and DRGs as intrinsically circadian tissues and reveal temporally structured molecular programs relevant to sensory processing and neuropathic pain.

papers.title: Noise or clearance? Reframing plasma amyloid-β variability in Alzheimer's disease as a measurable clearance signal.
papers.summary: This commentary argues that short-term variability in plasma amyloid-β 42/40 in Alzheimer's disease, recently reported to exceed 50% over five weeks in most participants, should not be dismissed solely as assay noise. The author proposes that dynamic brain-to-blood amyloid-β clearance, influenced by sleep and related physiological states, contributes to measured variability and suggests recording a bedside clearance-state index as a covariate.

papers.title: A Multi-Domain EEG Framework Integrating Spectral, Functional Connectivity, and Topological Features for Subject-Level ADHD Classification
papers.summary: The authors developed a subject-level EEG classification framework for ADHD integrating spectral features, wPLI functional connectivity, and persistent-homology topological descriptors, evaluated in 121 subjects with five classifiers. SVM achieved the best performance with 80.17% accuracy and 86.72% ROC-AUC, and ablation plus explainable AI analyses indicated that combined feature domains outperformed single-domain representations, with functional connectivity contributing most strongly.

papers.title: PRNP D178N-129MM prion disease: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease-like cortical ribboning without prominent early insomnia.
papers.summary: Reports a 59-year-old woman with PRNP D178N-129MM prion disease presenting with rapidly progressive cognitive-language decline and extensive cortical DWI ribboning without prominent early insomnia, plus a focused literature review of six previously reported D178N-129MM cases with prion-compatible cortical or cortical-striatal DWI abnormalities. Concludes that D178N-129MM disease shows substantial phenotypic and imaging heterogeneity, and that MRI pattern alone should not be used to infer a specific clinical phenotype.

papers.title: Combined Effect of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Preserved Ratio Impaired Spirometry on Cardiovascular Outcomes.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
keywords: major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events
papers.summary: Analyzed Sleep Heart Health Study data to test whether coexisting obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm) is associated with cardiovascular outcomes over a median 11.45-year follow-up. Found that OSA with PRISm was independently associated with increased major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (adjusted HR 1.52) and cardiovascular disease mortality (adjusted HR 2.17), with the association observed predominantly in women.

papers.title: Longitudinal associations between screen time activities and working memory neural signatures in adolescents: Sex differences and contextual moderation.
papers.summary: Longitudinal cohort study using Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study data (n=9931) to examine associations between screen media activities and working memory neural signature scores derived from EN-back fMRI, plus cognitive performance and mental health symptoms. Found that greater video gaming, texting, and television watching were associated with lower working memory neural signature scores, with male-specific associations and moderation by family conflict, sleep disturbance, and physical activity.

papers.title: Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharides alleviate cognitive impairment in sleep-deprived mice: Association with gut microbiota remodeling.
papers.summary: Tested whether Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharides (GLP) alleviate sleep deprivation-induced cognitive impairment in a chronic sleep deprivation mouse model, assessing behavior, hippocampal markers, 16S rRNA sequencing, and untargeted metabolomics. GLP improved memory and anxiety-like behaviors, increased hippocampal BDNF and synapse proteins PSD-95 and SYP, remodeled gut microbiota (enriching Kurthia and Roseburia, suppressing Escherichia-Shigella), and altered fecal metabolites, with correlations linking responsive taxa to behavioral and hippocampal outcomes.

papers.title: Inhaled β-myrcene alleviates insomnia in mice by modulating 5-HT1A/PKA signaling and the gut microbiota.
papers.summary: Investigated whether non-invasive inhalation of β-myrcene produces sedative-hypnotic effects in PCPA-induced insomnia mice and explored mechanisms involving 5-HT1A/PKA signaling and gut microbiota. Inhaled β-myrcene shortened sleep latency and prolonged sleep duration, reduced oxidative stress, modulated GABA, 5-HT, and glutamate levels, upregulated GABAARγ2, 5-HT1A, GAD65/67, and PKA, and correlated with altered gut microbiota composition.

papers.title: Regional alignment with sex-typical brain architecture, maternal health and environmental enrichment predict psychiatric symptoms in early life.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Used resting-state fMRI from 411 neonates (dHCP) and 214 children (Oregon ADHD 1000) to show that alignment with sex-typical functional connectivity patterns predicts psychiatric symptoms. Greater alignment with female-typical patterns predicted higher anxiety, while male-typical alignment predicted autism-related problems and ADHD/behavioral problems, with effects moderated by epigenetic age, maternal health, and environmental enrichment.

papers.title: LTPat-based SOXFE: A self-organized explainable feature engineering model for automated fibromyalgia detection.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.summary: The study evaluated a self-organized explainable feature engineering (SOXFE) model for EEG-based fibromyalgia classification using sleep EEG data, achieving record-wise leave-one-record-out (LORO) accuracy of 92.77% for NREM stage 2 and 97.00% for stage 3, with complementary segment-level 10-fold cross-validation reaching 100% accuracy; the authors caution that participant linkage was unavailable and subject-wise validation is needed.

papers.title: From Mechanistic Evidence to Clinical Translation: A Narrative Review of Chinese Herbal Medicine for Insomnia.
papers.summary: Narrative review evaluating Chinese herbal medicine for insomnia across five translational dimensions, including chemical characterization, exposure, mechanism, clinical endpoints, and safety. Preclinical evidence suggests effects via GABAergic and serotonergic signaling, HPA axis, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis-autophagy, and brain-gut-microbiota, but clinical studies are small, methodologically inconsistent, and lack long-term objective sleep and safety data.

papers.title: Non-motor correlates of anxiety in de novo Parkinson's disease: a cross-sectional study with exploratory subgroup analyses.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 284 drug-naïve de novo Parkinson's disease patients and 147 controls found clinically significant anxiety in 44.0% of patients versus 8.1% of controls. After adjustment, higher depressive symptoms were positively associated with anxiety, while better sleep quality and intact olfactory identification were negatively associated; a three-factor model achieved 84.81% classification accuracy.

papers.title: Age-dependent associations of sleep duration and insomnia symptoms with cognitive decline across five decades of adult life: a multi-cohort longitudinal study.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Multi-cohort longitudinal study of 16,884 participants examined age-dependent associations of sleep duration and insomnia symptoms with cognitive decline. Difficulty falling asleep was associated with faster 5-year decline in recall at age 50, with the association attenuating and reversing at older ages; similar age gradients replicated in Whitehall II and Rush MAP.

papers.title: Plasma Proteomic Landscape of Multidimensional Sleep Health and Its Association With Depression Risk Under Genetic Susceptibility.
papers.summary: Prospective cohort study of 36,852 UK Biobank participants identified 73 plasma proteins associated with multidimensional sleep health via elastic net regression. Healthy sleep and higher proteomic scores were associated with lower depression risk, and a significant additive interaction was observed between unhealthy sleep and high genetic risk for depression.

papers.title: Disability, Fatigue and Mental Health in Acute Versus Chronic Spinal Pain in the Gaza Strip: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: This comparative cross-sectional study of 410 adults with acute or chronic neck pain or low back pain in the Gaza Strip found that chronic spinal pain was associated with significantly higher disability, fatigue, and psychological distress than acute pain (p < 0.001), but sleep disturbance did not differ. Fatigue was independently associated with chronic pain status in both neck pain and LBP models.

papers.title: Complementing Engel Classification: Postoperative Scalp EEG as an Objective Indicator in SEEG-Guided Radiofrequency Thermocoagulation-A Seizure-Onset Pattern-Based Stratified Analysis.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 25 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing SEEG-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation, low-voltage fast activity (LVFA)-present seizure-onset patterns were associated with higher seizure freedom (92.3% vs 33.3%, p = 0.004) and postoperative scalp EEG normalization (87.5% vs 33.3%, p = 0.028) compared with LVFA-absent patterns. Postoperative EEG normalization may serve as an objective complement to Engel classification.

papers.title: Sleep trajectories in pregnancy: associations with trauma exposure, PTSD, and postpartum depression.
papers.summary: Using longitudinal growth mixture modeling across pregnancy and postpartum, this study identified two sleep trajectories: poor sleep (28.5%) and normative sleep (71.5%). Trauma-exposed participants with PTSD or other mental health conditions were more likely to have poor sleep profiles, and poor sleep profiles were associated with significantly higher postpartum depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Remimazolam ED95 for Preoperative Sedation in Children with Obstructive Sleep Apnea, with Obesity or a Reference-Range BMI: A Biased-Coin Dose-Finding Study.
papers.summary: This prospective biased-coin dose-finding study estimated the ED95 of remimazolam for preoperative sedation in children with obstructive sleep apnea and either obesity or reference-range BMI. ED95 was 0.38 mg/kg (95% CI 0.32–0.39) in the obesity group and 0.44 mg/kg (95% CI 0.39–0.44) in the reference-BMI group, with hypoxemia occurring in one child per group and bradycardia in one reference-BMI participant.

papers.title: Associations Between Weekly Commute Time, Weekday Sleep Duration, and Driving Fatigue Among Working Adults in Israel.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional analysis of 3,387 employed adults found that long weekly commuting (≥15 hours) was associated with insufficient sleep duration (OR=1.56) and driving fatigue (OR=1.71) among women, and with driving fatigue (OR=2.13) but not sleep duration among men. Gender-specific health behavior differences were also observed.

papers.title: Perioperative Anesthetic Considerations for Temporal Bone Tumor Resection in Fibroblast Growth Factor 23 (FGF23)-Related Tumor-Induced Osteomalacia: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes the perioperative anesthetic management of a 72-year-old male with FGF23-related tumor-induced osteomalacia undergoing temporal bone tumor resection. Intraoperative hypotension after induction required vasopressor support with ephedrine boluses and continuous phenylephrine infusion; the remainder of the procedure was uneventful.

papers.title: Melatonin supplementation in multiple sclerosis: a systematic review of clinical, imaging, biomarker, and safety outcomes.
papers.summary: Systematic review of 10 studies (435 participants) found that oral melatonin supplementation in adults with multiple sclerosis did not reduce relapse activity, disability progression, or new MRI lesions, though small inconsistent studies suggested possible improvements in sleep, fatigue, pain, cognition, mood, and inflammatory/oxidative biomarkers. High-dose melatonin (300 mg/day) was associated with hypertransaminasemia in three of four participants, and certainty of evidence was low or very low for all outcomes.

papers.title: Emotional State Evolution and Nursing Interventions in Patients Undergoing HSCT in Laminar Airflow Clean Rooms: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: Narrative review synthesizing evidence on emotional state evolution, associated distress factors, assessment approaches, and nursing interventions for patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in laminar airflow clean rooms, reporting that anxiety and uncertainty dominate pre-transplant and isolation entry while depressive symptoms increase during myelosuppression and prolonged isolation. Stronger empirical support was noted for inpatient palliative care, with emerging evidence for educational, relaxation, digital, and recreational interventions.

papers.title: Caregiver-Reported Behavioral Changes After Donepezil Transdermal Patch Therapy in Alzheimer's Disease: An Exploratory Real-World Network Analysis.
keywords: behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia
papers.summary: Exploratory retrospective single-center study of 26 Alzheimer's disease patients using caregiver-reported single-item change ratings and a descriptive co-improvement network, finding that smiling/positive affect (46.2%), calmness (34.6%), and night-time sleep (30.8%) were the most frequently improved behavioral domains after donepezil transdermal patch initiation. Calmness showed the highest observed strength centrality and remained highest in all leave-one-participant-out analyses, but findings are exploratory and do not establish efficacy.

papers.title: An evidence-informed occupational health curriculum for pre-deployment preparation of aquanauts in underwater habitats: a scenario-based framework development study.
papers.summary: Developed a scenario-based, evidence-informed occupational health curriculum for pre-deployment preparation of non-medical aquanauts in a 15-m underwater habitat for 14 days, specifying four domains, ten modules, and 28 observable learning outcomes covering emergency preparedness, physical self-maintenance, psychological/team functioning, and underwater operational safety. The framework is preliminary and unvalidated, with no Delphi round or validation study performed.

papers.title: The Use of Montelukast in Pediatric Asthma and Anti-Inflammatory Effects - Easy Choice or a Balancing Act?
papers.summary: Review of montelukast as a selective cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 1 antagonist in pediatric asthma and allergic rhinitis, reporting that it reduces markers of allergic inflammation such as fractional exhaled nitric oxide, eosinophilia, adhesion molecules, and selected cytokines. It supports use mainly as an add-on controller or alternative when corticosteroids are contraindicated, with caution warranted due to consistently reported milder sleep-related and behavioral neuropsychiatric symptoms.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
